results.template:
BEFORE ESCALATING — Order Fraud
Source: KB Ashry.docx (Before Escalating)

Required steps / info to collect:
Step 1 : Check the customer account’s recent order status.
• Go to CS Hub from the Customer Detail >click on Histories > and check the Status. Step 2 : Depending on the order status you have two different resolutions: IF The order status is Not Active: Order (expired) = Go to step 3 IF The order is Active: Order (approved), Order (authorised), or Order (fully_captured) = Go to step 4 | Step 3 (Order is Expired): 1- Click the order and check the order information (order number, store name, customer's first name, | and phone number last 4 digits). | 2- Provide the customer with the below info.:
• Last 4 digits of the user phone number
• If the first name in the shipping info. is different, you can provide the customer with that as well.
• Advise the customer that the order is not active which means there are no dues.
• Educate them on the importance of not sharing any information with others, like the account’s phone number, OTP, passcodes, and all information.
• Add a case comment with case details
• Issue type Payment > Unrecognized charge > Explained to customer (no issue)
Step 4 : The order is “ Active” --> Order (approved), Order (authorised), or Order (fully_captured) | 1- Check the order information (order number, store name, customer's first name, and phone number's last 4 digits). 2- Provide all information to your customer, as they may recognize the person and they can contact them personally.
3- If they don’t recognize the person, this is a potential fraud case, escalate it to the Trust & Safety team by following the steps in [Customer/Merchant] Transferring Sales Force Cases for further investigation.
4- Ask the customer the below questions
Q1- When did this happen?
Q2- How did someone get your national ID/iqama number?
Q3- An OTP is sent to your phone number from Absher to activate your account. Why did you give it away?
Q4- Who is the person that you give your information to?
Q5- There is an OTP sent to complete the order and it says for purchase why did you give it away?
Q6- Maybe it's one of your friends or family that has been using your account?
Q7- If not who do you suspect?
Q8- Ask if he did file a report to the police.
Q9- What is the phone number of the caller?
• If the customer’s phone number was stolen, they can provide a police report/proof | as evidence.
5- Once you receive answers from the customer, add all case details in a case comments and escalate to the Trust & Safety team.Issue type Payment > Unrecognized charge > Suspected fraud

Add all answers in the case comment, then escalate with the correct Issue Type / Team / SLA.
